title: Virtual Environment
test_conventions: Tests are Python assert snippets run AFTER the learner's code in the same namespace. The learner's stdout is available to tests as the string variable __stdout__. expected_output comparisons are exact after stripping trailing whitespace on each line. Tests with visible:false are hidden and each carries a failure_message. Everything runs offline in Pyodide; no input(), network or pip. The learner's own source code is also available to tests as the string variable __source__ (use it for AST/source checks that catch hard-coded answers).

exercises.code:
text = '''Click==7.0
Flask==1.1.1
Jinja2==2.10.3'''
packages = {}
for line in text.split('\n'):
    name, version = line.split('==')
    packages[name] = version
print(packages['Flask'], len(packages))
exercises.explanation: The loop stores name -> version for each of the 3 lines. packages['Flask'] is '1.1.1' and the dict has 3 entries.

misconceptions.Flask 3: The dict maps the name to the version, so packages['Flask'] is the version string.
misconceptions.1.1.1 2: Every line adds a key; there are three different names, so len is 3.
misconceptions.7.0 3: 7.0 is the version of Click. We asked for the key 'Flask'.

exercises.explanation_tr: Döngü 3 satırın her biri için isim -> sürüm kaydeder. packages['Flask'] '1.1.1' olur ve dict'te 3 kayıt vardır.

misconceptions_tr.Flask 3: Dict isimi sürüme eşler, bu yüzden packages['Flask'] sürüm metnidir.
misconceptions_tr.1.1.1 2: Her satır bir anahtar ekler; üç farklı isim var, yani len 3'tür.

worked_example.code:
active = True
venv, system = [], []
target = venv if active else system
target.append('Flask')
print(venv, system)
notes: An active virtual environment receives the installs; otherwise they go to the system Python.
The (venv) prefix in the prompt tells you the environment is active.
notes_tr: Aktif bir sanal ortam kurulumları alır; aktif değilse kurulumlar sistem Python'una gider.
Komut satırındaki (venv) öneki, ortamın aktif olduğunu gösterir.

exercises.explanation: numpy was installed while active was False, so it went to the global list. After active = True, Flask went to the environment list.

misconceptions.[] ['numpy', 'Flask']: The environment was not active when numpy was installed, so numpy went to the global list.
misconceptions.['numpy', 'Flask'] []: After sh.active = True the installs go to the environment list.
misconceptions.['Flask'] ['numpy']: You swapped the lists: inactive installs go to global_packages, active ones to venv_packages.

exercises.explanation_tr: numpy, active False iken kuruldu, bu yüzden global listeye gitti. active = True olduktan sonra Flask ortam listesine gitti.

misconceptions_tr.[] ['numpy', 'Flask']: numpy kurulurken ortam aktif değildi, bu yüzden numpy global listeye gitti.

misconceptions_tr.['Flask'] ['numpy']: Listeleri karıştırdın: aktif olmayan kurulumlar global_packages'a, aktif olanlar venv_packages'a gider.

exercises.prompt: In your own words: why do we create a virtual environment for each project, and what does (venv) in the prompt tell you?
exercises.prompt_tr: Kendi cümlelerinle anlat: neden her proje için sanal ortam oluştururuz ve komut satırındaki (venv) neyi gösterir?
exercises.model_answer: A virtual environment is an isolated copy of Python with its own installed packages, so one project's dependencies cannot conflict with another's. The (venv) prefix in the prompt shows that the environment is active, so pip install puts packages there.
exercises.model_answer_tr: Sanal ortam, kendi kurulu paketleri olan yalıtılmış bir Python kopyasıdır; böylece bir projenin bağımlılıkları (dependencies) başka bir projeninkiyle çakışmaz. Komut satırındaki (venv) öneki ortamın aktif olduğunu gösterir, yani pip install paketleri oraya kurar.

exercises.prompt: Write should_track(path, ignore_lines). It returns False when path starts with any entry of ignore_lines, otherwise True.
exercises.prompt_tr: should_track(path, ignore_lines) yaz. path, ignore_lines içindeki herhangi bir girişle başlıyorsa False, değilse True döndürsün.

tests.failure_message: With an empty ignore list every file is tracked.

tests.failure_message: Only paths that START with the entry are ignored; 'myvenv/' is a different folder.
tests.failure_message_tr: Yalnızca girişle BAŞLAYAN yollar yok sayılır; 'myvenv/' başka bir klasördür.

tests.code: assert should_track('node_modules/a.js', ['venv/', 'node_modules/']) is False and should_track('lib/x.py', ['venv/', 'node_modules/']) is True
tests.failure_message: The result must come from the ignore list you are given: any matching entry means False. Do not return a fixed value.
tests.failure_message_tr: Sonuç, verilen ignore listesine bağlı olmalı: eşleşen herhangi bir giriş False demektir. Sabit bir değer döndürme.

hints: Check each ignore entry against the beginning of the path.
str.startswith(entry) does exactly that; any(...) combines the results.
Last step: return the opposite (not) of any(...) over the entries, where each test is path.startswith(___).

solution.code:
def should_track(path, ignore_lines):
    return not any(path.startswith(p) for p in ignore_lines)

hints_tr: Her ignore girişini yolun başıyla karşılaştır.
str.startswith(giriş) tam olarak bunu yapar; any(...) sonuçları birleştirir.
Son adım: girişler üzerinde any(...) ifadesinin tersini (not) döndür; her test path.startswith(___) olsun.

solution.code:
def tracked_files(paths, ignore_lines):
    return [p for p in paths if not any(p.startswith(i) for i in ignore_lines)]
solution.approach_tr: Listeyi bir liste kapsamı ile filtrele.
